hints: Use the generalized binomial expansion for \((1+u)^{1/3}\), with \(u=6x\).
Substitute \(u=6x\) and simplify each coefficient separately, keeping terms only through \(x^3\).
walkthrough:
Recall the general binomial series for $(1 + u)^n$ where $n = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $u = 6x$:
$$(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!}u^3 + \dots$$

Calculate the coefficients of the powers of $u$:
$$\text{For } u: \quad n = \dfrac{1}{3}$$
$$\text{For } u^2: \quad \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)}{2} = \dfrac{-\frac{2}{9}}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{9}$$
$$\text{For } u^3: \quad \dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)}{6} = \dfrac{\frac{10}{27}}{6} = \dfrac{10}{162} = \dfrac{5}{81}$$

Simplify the terms through elementary arithmetic:
$$\text{Term 1: } 1$$
$$\text{Term 2: } \dfrac{1}{3} \times 6x = 2x$$
$$\text{Term 3: } -\dfrac{1}{9} \times 36x^2 = -4x^2$$
$$\text{Term 4: } \dfrac{5}{81} \times 216x^3 = 5 \times \dfrac{216}{81}x^3 = 5 \times \dfrac{8}{3}x^3 = \dfrac{40}{3}x^3$$

hints: For a non-integer binomial expansion of \((1+u)^{1/3}\), the convergence condition is \(|u|<1\).
Here \(u=6x\), so apply the condition to \(|6x|\) and retain the strict inequality.
walkthrough:
State the condition of convergence for the binomial series of $(1 + u)^n$ when $n$ is not a positive integer:
$$|u| < 1$$

Substitute the argument $u = 6x$ into the condition:
$$|6x| < 1$$
